page.layout: One page of running text in a single block; no marginal notes, no running head. Below the last line: a gathering signature at the left and a catchword at the right.

main_text.p: despici,& viros illos quamuis magnos tradu-ci temere,tanquam si aut in ea solum re versa-ti essent aut ad alias ineptiores essent, & se im-pares oneri huic esse facto suo plane fateretur. Quod genus criminationis re & veritate fal-sum opiniones tamen imperiti vulgi & eorum qui dissentiunt occupat incessitq; facilime. Hæc cogitatio, ut alias taceam, multis iamdiu instantibus eo me adduxit, ut ad disputationes Bellarmini examinandas & pro veritate Dei in Scripturis comprehensa confutandas ve-niens,ijsdem cancellis quos manus ipsius po-suit labyrinthum errorum, quos conscuit co-pia maxima, Ariadneo, et potius diuino sacræ Scripturæ filo ductus percurrerem, facerem-que testatum bonis, quæ ab ipso dicuntur be-ne,nos religione maxima & Christiana sim-plicitate optime acquiescere; quæ secus ea nos sine iracundia, peruicacia, aut contumelia (q[?] Christianis pectoribus indignum) refellere. Atq; huius studij & laboris mei partes aliquot in lucem publicam his paucis annis prodierunt, ut ædificationi publicæ pro modulo meo, quæ[?] Christus mihi admetitur, Christiana veritate & simplicitate confulerem, sperans & confi-dens in Domino, ut tum hoc facto meo mul-tæ Christianæ animæ falso dispungedo, & ve-se[?] agnoscendo amplectendoq;[?] reddantur ap-tio

page.notes: Uncertain readings: "(q[?]" (abbreviation before "Christianis", possibly quod); "quæ[?]" (a letter shaped like a ligature after "pro modulo meo,"); "se[?]" at the start of the last full line, after the hyphen "ve-"; "amplectendoq;[?]" (the "ct" ligature is hard to read at this resolution). "conscuit" is read as printed, though the letters may be "conscuit" or "consecuit". The word "tio" is the catchword, the start of the next page's first word, and is therefore not repeated in the text. The "X 4" at the foot is the gathering signature, not a page number.
